candidates.original_title: Default neglect in attempts at social influence
candidates.description: In Study 1h, choice architects selecting a default to influence a new employee toward a higher-paying or more vacation-rich job selected the optimal default at below-chance levels.
candidates.citation_sentence: Experiment 2 includes both a direct and a conceptual replication of Zlatev et al.'s (2017) Study 1h.
candidates.notes: The conceptual replication simplified the task and removed the default-framing confound; optimal-default selection was significantly above chance, which the authors describe as the opposite pattern and a reversal of the original result. candidates.original_title: Default neglect in attempts at social influence
candidates.description: In Study 1h, choice architects selecting a default to influence a new employee toward a higher-paying or more vacation-rich job selected the optimal default at below-chance levels when the option attributes were framed as the advantages and disadvantages of switching jobs.
candidates.citation_sentence: First, we again replicated Zlatev et al.'s (2017) original results when the (dis)advantages were framed in terms of switching to the new job.
candidates.notes: Experiment 3 tested both the original switch framing and an alternate stay framing within one experiment; results were below chance in the original framing and above chance in the alternate framing, so the entry is inconclusive under the multi-condition rule.
